title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
This page finishes a case analysis of uniformization for conformal (Riemann) surfaces with boundary, using the Schottky double. The setup, carried over from the previous pages, is as follows.

- X is a conformal surface with boundary.
- 𝒳 is a simply connected conformal surface without boundary (the double, or a covering of it).
- σ is an antiholomorphic involution of 𝒳 that has fixed points.
- The fixed locus of σ becomes the boundary ∂X of X = 𝒳/σ.

The previous page treated case a′. There 𝒳 ≅ ℂ and σ is reflection in a real affine line. The quotient is the closed half-plane H̄ = {Im z ≥ 0}. Its automorphism group is the real affine group, and its flat metrics, taken up to constants, form one Aut-orbit.

This page treats case b′. Here 𝒳 ≅ ℙ¹_ℂ and σ is an 'inversion', i.e. reflection in a circle. Such a σ is the same thing as a real structure on ℙ¹ with real points, i.e. a structure of real projective line. The quotient X is a closed disk.

A 'distinguished' metric means a constant-curvature metric compatible with the conformal structure. On ℙ¹ these are the round metrics. They form PSL₂(ℂ)/PSU(2) ≅ hyperbolic 3-space, so they depend on 3 real parameters. The σ-invariant ones correspond to the σ-fixed points of that space, namely PSL₂(ℝ)/SO(2) ≅ the open hyperbolic disk. So giving a σ-invariant round metric is the same as choosing a point of the open disk X∖∂X, the centre of the hemisphere.

The summary on the page states the result. A simply connected conformal surface, with or without boundary, has a unique distinguished metric: the complete hyperbolic one, with the boundary geodesic, obtained via the double. There are four exceptions:

- (a) ℂ and (a′) H̄ have flat metrics. These are unique up to a multiplicative constant and form a single orbit under Aut X.
- (b) ℙ¹ and (b′) the closed disk have spherical metrics. These form 3-parameter and 2-parameter real families respectively, each a single Aut X-orbit.

The next page goes on to hyperbolicity criteria for open subsets (Picard-type exceptions) and to non-orientable surfaces. The non-orientable cases arise as quotients by fixed-point-free anti-involutions (ℝP², Möbius band, Klein bottle and so on).
errors: No mathematical error. The parameter counts are correct: dim_ℝ PSL₂(ℂ)/PSU(2) = 3 and dim_ℝ PSL₂(ℝ)/SO(2) = 2. The orbit statements are also correct.

The hyperbolic 'unique distinguished metric' claim relies on a normalization of curvature (−1), which is implicit. In the hyperbolic case with boundary, the metric is the one from the double, so ∂X is geodesic; this is likewise unstated.
'Closed disk' must be understood as including its boundary circle. Otherwise it would not be an exceptional case.

ideas.what: Uniformization of bordered simply connected Riemann surfaces via the Schottky double with an antiholomorphic involution. The exceptional cases are the closed half-plane and the closed disk.
ideas.modern_name: Schottky double / uniformization of bordered Riemann surfaces (Klein surfaces)

ideas.what: Moduli of distinguished constant-curvature metrics on exceptional cases as homogeneous spaces: H³ for ℙ¹ and H² for the disk with a real structure.
ideas.modern_name: Space of round metrics on the sphere ≅ hyperbolic 3-space; fixed points of a real structure ≅ H²

ideas.what: A real structure (inversion) on ℙ¹_ℂ is equivalent to a real projective line structure on the boundary.
ideas.modern_name: Real forms of ℙ¹ / circles in the Riemann sphere

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, correct but classical classification of the exceptional (non-hyperbolic) simply connected bordered conformal surfaces and their canonical metrics. It is interesting only as part of Grothendieck's unpublished 'chirurgie des surfaces conformes' framework, which is related in spirit to the 'surfaces à bord' and real-structure themes of Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: 'σ-connexe' at the start of the summary is most likely '1-connexe' (simply connected). The list of exceptions (ℂ, H̄, ℙ¹, closed disk) is exactly the simply connected one.
'Hc [?] surface conforme' is probably 'Toute surface conforme'.
'métrique dimensionnelle [?] distinguée' is probably 'métrique riemannienne distinguée'.
The half-plane in the summary should be the closed one, H̄ = {z ∈ ℂ | Im z ≥ 0}, with bar notation as on the previous page.
The last line reads approximately: 'il y a alors un ens. de métriques distinguées dépendant de 3 paramètres réels resp. de 2 paramètres réels, également orbites sous Aut X'.
